working_title: Night Prayer Before Sleep | Give God Your Worries, Rest in His Peace
promise: Title promise 'give God your worries and rest in his peace' is spoken at 0-8 s.
angle: For the listener whose body is tired but whose mind will not stop: cast every care on the God who never sleeps, receive forgiveness, and lie down in peace.
authorship: Original text written for HeroVerse by Claude Code (AI assistant) on 2026-10-18. Scripture quotations are from the King James Version (public domain).

segments.beat: 0-8 s: direct address, concrete moment, promise
segments.text: Good evening. If your body is tired but your mind will not stop, stay with me for the next few minutes. Before you sleep tonight, you can hand every worry to God and rest in his peace. Take one slow breath with me.

segments.beat: 8-30 s: settle the body, name the need
segments.text: Let your head sink into the pillow. Let your jaw relax, and your shoulders, and your hands. The day is finished. Whatever was left undone can wait until morning. Right now you are invited to do only one thing: to rest in the presence of the God who never sleeps, so that you can.
King David wrote this at the end of a hard day. I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.

segments.beat: reflection: safety is his job tonight
segments.text: Notice who keeps David safe. Not the locks on the door. Not his own planning. Thou, Lord, only. Your safety tonight is not something you have to guard by staying awake. It is something God does for you while you sleep.

So let us pray. Lord, I come to you at the end of this day. You saw all of it, the good moments and the hard ones, the things I did well and the things I wish I could do again. I bring it all to you now. Quiet my heart, and let me lie down in your peace.
Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

To cast something is to throw it, to let it leave your hands. Not to set it down beside the bed so you can pick it up again at three in the morning. And the reason is the most tender line in the verse: for he careth for you. God is not tired of your worries. He wants them.

Father, I name my worries before you now. The one about money. The one about my health. The one about someone I love. The conversation that went badly. The thing I am afraid will happen tomorrow. One by one, I open my hands and give them to you. I cannot solve them tonight. You can hold them while I sleep.

Jesus said, Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

segments.beat: reflection: rest for the soul, not only the body
segments.text: Jesus promises rest for your souls. Sleep can rest your body, but only he can rest the part of you that keeps running even when your eyes are closed. He is gentle and humble in heart. You do not have to perform for him tonight. You only have to come.
Let us be still. Breathe in slowly. And breathe out. Once more, breathe in, and let the whole day go.

segments.beat: turn: examining the day with grace
segments.text: Now let us look back over this day with God, gently, and without fear.

segments.beat: guided prayer: thanksgiving for the day
segments.text: Thank you, Lord, for the gifts of today. For food on the table, for the people who spoke kindly to me, for the work I could do, for every small mercy I did not even notice at the time. Thank you that I made it through. Even on the hardest days, you were with me in every hour.

Father, I also bring you what I regret. The impatient word. The thing I should have done and did not. The moment I chose myself over someone else. I do not want to carry guilt into my sleep. I confess it to you honestly, and I receive your forgiveness.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

segments.beat: reflection: a clean slate before sleep
segments.text: Faithful and just. God does not forgive you reluctantly. He forgives you because he promised he would, and he always keeps his promises. So tonight you can lay your head down clean. Tomorrow does not have to begin with yesterday's weight.

Lord, if there is anyone I am angry with tonight, help me to release it before I sleep. If I have hurt someone, show me how to make it right tomorrow. Soften my heart toward the people in my home. Let love, not resentment, be the last thing in my mind tonight.
Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath.
He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.

segments.beat: reflection: someone stays awake for you
segments.text: There is a quiet comfort in this. When you close your eyes, God does not close his. He keeps watch over you all night long. You can let go of control, because the One who holds the world is wide awake.

segments.beat: guided prayer: protection through the night
segments.text: Lord, watch over me and my home tonight. Guard the doors and the windows. Protect every person sleeping under this roof, and those I love who are far away. Keep away every danger, every fear, and every harmful thing. Let your angels stand watch until morning.

He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler. Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day.

segments.beat: guided prayer: fear in the dark
segments.text: Father, for anyone who feels afraid when the lights go out, I ask for your nearness. Calm the racing heart. Quiet the thoughts that grow louder in the dark. Let them feel covered, like a child under a warm blanket, safe under your wings.

If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me. Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.

segments.beat: reflection: night is not dark to God
segments.text: To you the night may feel long and heavy. To God, it shines like the day. He sees you as clearly at midnight as he did at noon. Nothing that happens in the dark is hidden from him, and nothing in the dark can separate you from his love.

Lord, I give you my thoughts. When my mind starts replaying the day or rehearsing tomorrow, bring it back to you. Replace every anxious thought with a promise from your word. Let my last thoughts tonight be thoughts of your goodness.
Jesus said, Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

segments.beat: guided prayer: the body and sleep
segments.text: Father, I give you my body. Heal what hurts. Ease the tension in my muscles. Slow my breathing and my heartbeat. Give me deep, restful sleep, the kind that truly restores. And if I wake in the night, let my first thought be of you, and help me to fall asleep again.
When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.

segments.beat: guided prayer: the ones awake tonight
segments.text: And Lord, I pray for everyone who cannot sleep tonight. Those in hospital beds. Those working the night shift. Those sitting beside someone who is sick. Those grieving in a quiet house. Be close to each of them. Give them strength for the night and hope for the morning.
For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.

segments.beat: reflection: the night is not the end
segments.text: Weeping may endure for a night. But the night is not the end. Joy comes in the morning. Whatever is heavy tonight, you do not have to resolve it before you sleep. God will meet you again when the sun rises.

segments.beat: guided prayer: the people I love
segments.text: Lord, I lift up the people I love before I sleep. My family, my friends, the ones who make my life richer and the ones I worry about most. Wherever they are tonight, cover them with your peace. Heal what is broken between us. Let each of them feel, even in their sleep, that they are deeply loved by you.

Father, I pray for the children, ours and every child who will sleep tonight. Give them sweet dreams and safe rooms. Keep fear and nightmares far from them. Let them grow up knowing that you watch over them, every night of their lives.

Lord, I give you the needs I lay awake thinking about. The bills, the rent, the job, the plans that depend on things I cannot control. You feed the birds of the air and clothe the lilies of the field. I trust you to provide for me tomorrow, as you have provided for me today.

And Father, for anyone who feels lonely in the quiet of the night, or who misses someone who is no longer beside them, draw near. Hold the empty space with them. Let them sense your presence in the room, closer than their own breath.

segments.beat: guided prayer: tomorrow in his hands
segments.text: Father, I place tomorrow in your hands. I do not know everything it will bring, but I know you will already be there. I will not worry about it tonight. When I wake, I will meet you there.

Lord, as I rest in safety, I remember those who do not. People in places of war, families without a home tonight, refugees far from everything familiar. Protect them. Provide for them. Bring peace to the nations, and use me tomorrow to be part of your answer.

And now, Father, I surrender this night to you. My plans, my fears, my hopes, my unfinished business. All of it is yours. I stop holding on. I let you hold me instead. Into your hands I commit my spirit, as I fall asleep.
It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.

Now let me read a psalm over you, slowly, as you rest. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

segments.beat: reflection: he makes me lie down
segments.text: He maketh me to lie down. The shepherd knows when the sheep need rest, even when they keep wandering. Tonight he is leading you beside still waters. Let him restore your soul while you sleep.
Breathe in again, slowly. And let it out. Let your body grow heavy and still.
Say these words with me quietly, as you rest. I am safe in God's hands. I am forgiven. I am loved. My worries belong to him tonight. He gives his beloved sleep, and I am his beloved.
When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches.

segments.beat: payoff: one concrete commitment for tonight
segments.text: Here is one thing to do tonight. If you wake up in the dark and a worry comes back, do not argue with it. Simply say, Lord, this is yours, and turn over and rest. He is awake. You can sleep.

segments.beat: soft call to action before the sleep section
segments.text: If this prayer is bringing you peace, type amen in the comments now, so others can pray with you. Then stay right where you are. For the rest of this time, I will read Scripture over you slowly, so you can drift off to sleep resting in God's word.

Let us begin by letting the body rest. Breathe in slowly through your nose, and let the breath out through your mouth, a little longer than it came in. Feel the weight of your head on the pillow. Let your forehead smooth out. Let your eyes grow heavy. Let your jaw loosen, and your tongue rest. You are safe. You are held.

Now let your shoulders sink down into the bed. Let the tension in your neck melt away. Let your arms grow heavy, from the shoulders to the elbows, from the elbows to the wrists, all the way to the tips of your fingers. Open your hands a little, as if you were giving the whole day back to God. There is nothing left to hold.

Let your breathing slow down on its own. Feel your chest rise and fall, gently, without effort. Let your stomach relax. Let your legs grow heavy and warm, from your hips to your knees, from your knees to your ankles, all the way down to your feet. Your whole body is resting now. And the Lord who made it is watching over you.

Listen to the psalm of the God who keeps you. I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth. He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep. The LORD is thy keeper: the LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand. The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night. The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul. The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.

The Lord is thy keeper. Not only in the daytime, when you can see what is coming, but in the night, when you cannot. Not the moon by night. Even the darkness is under his care. Let that word settle over you: kept. Tonight you are kept.

Now hear the words of Jesus about worry. Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment? Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they? Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature? And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith? Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed? For after all these things do the Gentiles seek: for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things. But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

segments.beat: sleep reflection: the birds are sleeping too
segments.text: Somewhere tonight the birds Jesus spoke about are asleep in their nests. They did not plan tomorrow's food. They simply rest, and the Father feeds them. You are worth far more to him than they are. Tomorrow will take care of itself. For now, only rest.
Father, I give you tomorrow. Every meeting, every bill, every conversation, every unknown. I do not need to solve any of it tonight. You know what I need before I ask. I rest in that.

Jesus said to his friends on the night before he died, Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me. In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.
segments.chapter: Let not your heart be troubled (John 14:1-3)

segments.text: On the hardest night of his life, Jesus spent his words comforting others. Let not your heart be troubled. He has prepared a place for you, and he is preparing you for it. Even this night, even this rest, is part of his care.

Hear the prophet Isaiah. Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding. He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength. Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

segments.beat: sleep reflection: he never grows tired
segments.text: The everlasting God fainteth not, neither is weary. You grow tired, and that is human. He never does. So you can let your strength run out tonight. While you sleep, he is renewing it.
Breathe in slowly. And let it go. Rest in the quiet.

The apostle Paul wrote these words from a prison cell. Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.

segments.beat: sleep reflection: think on these things
segments.text: As you fall asleep, let your mind rest on what is lovely. A kind word someone said to you today. The face of someone you love. The goodness of God that brought you to this moment. Think on these things, and let the peace that passes understanding stand guard over your heart.

Hear these words of assurance. Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us. For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

segments.beat: sleep reflection: nothing can separate you
segments.text: Nothing. Not the things you did today. Not the things that worry you about tomorrow. Not the darkness of this night. Nothing in all creation can separate you from the love of God. Rest in that love now.
Lord, thank you that your love does not depend on how well I did today. Hold me in that love as I sleep. And hold the people I love, wherever they are tonight.

It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness. The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him. The LORD is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD.

segments.beat: sleep reflection: mercy waiting for the morning
segments.text: When you wake, fresh mercy will already be there, waiting for you, new every morning. Tonight you only need to do what the prophet says: hope, and quietly wait.

Listen to the psalm of the God who knows you completely. O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me. Thou knowest my downsitting and mine uprising, thou understandest my thought afar off. Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways. For there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O LORD, thou knowest it altogether. Thou hast beset me behind and before, and laid thine hand upon me. Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain unto it. Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence? If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there. If I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea; Even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me.

segments.beat: sleep reflection: he knows your lying down
segments.text: Thou compassest my lying down. God knows exactly where you are lying tonight, and how you feel as you lie there. His hand is upon you. There is nowhere you could go, not even into sleep, where he is not with you.
Let your breathing slow even more. You are safe. Rest.

Now let me read the whole of Psalm ninety-one over you. He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust. Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence. He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler. Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday. A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked. Because thou hast made the LORD, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation; There shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling. For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone. Thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder: the young lion and the dragon shalt thou trample under feet. Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name. He shall call upon me, and I will answer him: I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honour him. With long life will I satisfy him, and shew him my salvation.

The secret place of the Most High is not far away. It is wherever you turn your heart toward him, even here, even in this bed, even half asleep. Abide there tonight, under the shadow of the Almighty. He shall call upon me, and I will answer him. He hears you.

My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him. He only is my rock and my salvation: he is my defence; I shall not be moved. In God is my salvation and my glory: the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God. Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us.

segments.beat: sleep reflection: pour out your heart
segments.text: Pour out your heart before him. Whatever is still left in you tonight, the last worry, the last sadness, pour it out. He is your rock. You can lean your whole weight on him, and he will not move.

I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved. Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope. Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.

segments.beat: sleep reflection: my flesh shall rest in hope
segments.text: My flesh also shall rest in hope. Your body can rest tonight, not because every problem is solved, but because your hope is in God. He is at your right hand. You will not be moved.
Lord, as sleep comes, I place myself completely in your hands. My body, my mind, my heart, my family, my tomorrow. Watch over me through the night, and wake me to your mercy in the morning.

segments.beat: closing blessing (end of the sleep section)
segments.text: And now receive this blessing as you sleep. Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord be with you all. Sleep well, in the shelter of his love. In Jesus' name, amen.

description_intro: Tired body, racing mind? Give God every worry tonight, then fall asleep to Scripture read slowly over you: Psalm 91, Psalm 121, Psalm 23, Matthew 6 and more.
